Please note the following before viewing the unofficial election results:

  1. D=Democratic R=Republican L=Libertarian UK=United Kansas i=independent
  2. The unofficial results that appear are exactly as reported by county election officials.
  3. These unofficial results on election night are incomplete and do not include provisional ballots.
  4. Provisional ballots will be counted during the county canvass no later than November 16, 2026
  5. These results are unofficial until the State Board of Canvassers certify the results of the General Election on December 1, 2026, deeming the results official.

This page will be updated beginning 7:00pm CST Tuesday, November 3, 2026, through end of day Friday, November 6, 2026.

Step by Step Election Cycle

STEP 1: ELECTION NIGHT

Election night results are unofficial results and do not and will not include county canvass certified results, provisional ballots, or votes from write-in candidates. Final official results will be posted on the Secretary of State’s website after the State Board of Canvassers.

STEP 2: POST-ELECTION AUDIT

The Secretary of State shall randomly select races to be audited in each county. The selection will take place at 9 a.m. following election day.

The Secretary of State will notify each county election office of the races to be audited as well as the constitutional amendment. The county election office will randomly select the precincts to be audited for each race. The audit shall then be performed manually by the counties and shall review all paper ballots selected to ensure the hand count is identical to the vote count from the tabulators. The audit shall be performed by a sworn election board consisting of bipartisan, trained board members. Please contact your county election office for your official county audit results.

REMINDER - Every vote cast by a voter in Kansas results in a paper ballot submitted by the voter and is subject to the audit.

Audits must be completed before the county canvass.

STEP 2A: (POTENTIAL) CLOSE-RACE AUDIT

If a federal, statewide, or state legislative race is within 1% of the total votes tallied on election night, a close-race audit is triggered in addition to the required post-election audit. During even-numbered election years, the county election officer shall conduct the close-race audit in an additional 10% of the county’s precincts for the specified race, with a minimum of an additional one precinct audited in each county.

STEP 3: COUNTY CANVASS

The County Board of Canvassers consists of the elected county commissioners in each county. The responsibility of the County Board of Canvassers is to review and determine the outcome of all provisional ballots, include the provisional ballot vote totals with the election results and certify the final election results within the county. The canvassing takes place publicly and must be completed between six and thirteen days following the election. Certification of primary and general election results by the County Board of Canvassers is required for all elections.

STEP 4: (OPTIONAL) RECOUNT

The recount law was enacted in 1978. A recount must be requested not later than 5 p.m. on the day following the certification of the election by the County Board of Canvassers and can occur in a candidate or constitutional amendment election. In a multi-county district, the recount request must be submitted after the last county has certified the results. The person requesting the recount must specify the area and manner of recount and must post a bond covering the cost of the recount before the recount may begin.

In the general election the state will cover the cost of a recount done in the same manner as Election Day if the race is within ½%.

STEP 5: STATE BOARD OF CANVASSERS

The State Board of Canvassers consists of the Governor, Secretary of State, and Attorney General or their designees. The State Board of Canvassers meets following the certification by the County Boards of Canvassers of the election results in each county. The State Board of Canvassers is responsible for certifying the primary and general election results for all national and state offices, and constitutional amendments. The meeting takes place publicly and must be completed no later than the first business day of the following month. Certification of election results by the State Board of Canvassers is required for all primary and general races for national and state offices, and constitutional amendments.

ELECTION RESULTS ARE NOW OFFICIAL
